ros: In ROS 1, which command starts the Master together with the parameter server and the rosout logging node?
roscore
rosnode start master
rosrun roscore master
rostopic init
roscore launches the Master, the parameter server and rosout in one step. The other commands do not exist in this form.
In ROS 1, what does the Master do after a publisher and a subscriber on the same topic have found each other?
Nothing for that data: messages flow directly between the two nodes
It relays every message from the publisher to the subscriber
It buffers messages until the subscriber explicitly requests them
It serializes each message and stores a copy for later replay
The Master only provides naming and lookup. Once nodes know each other's addresses, they connect peer to peer over TCPROS or UDPROS.
Which terminal command publishes one std_msgs/String message to the /chatter topic in ROS 1?
rostopic pub -1 /chatter std_msgs/String "data: 'hi'"
rosservice call /chatter std_msgs/String "data: 'hi'"
rosmsg pub -1 /chatter std_msgs/String "data: 'hi'"
rosnode pub -1 /chatter std_msgs/String "data: 'hi'"
rostopic pub publishes to a topic, and -1 publishes once and exits. rosservice call is for services, and rosmsg only shows message definitions.
In a custom ROS .msg file, what does the line float64[] ranges declare?
A variable-length array of 64-bit floats named ranges
A fixed-length array of 64 floats named ranges
A single 64-bit float named ranges with a default value
A reference to another message type called ranges
Empty brackets mean an unbounded array. A fixed-size array would be written with a number inside, such as float64[3].
A rospy subscriber uses queue_size=1 and its callback is slower than the publisher. What happens?
Older messages are dropped and the callback gets the newest one
The publisher blocks until the subscriber has finished
Messages pile up in memory until the node runs out of RAM
The node shuts down with a queue overflow exception
With a small queue, ROS discards older messages when new ones arrive. This is a common choice for sensor data where only the latest value matters.
A ROS node must ask a planner to compute one path and wait for the reply. Which communication mechanism fits best?
A service, which gives a request and a matching response
A topic with a queue size of 1 on both ends
A parameter written to the parameter server
A bag file that the planner replays on demand
Services implement synchronous request and response. Topics are one-way streams with no built-in reply, and parameters are for configuration.
In a ROS .srv file, what separates the request fields from the response fields?
A line containing three dashes: ---
A blank line between the two groups
A line containing three equals signs: ===
A comment line that reads #response
The --- separator splits a .srv definition into request (above) and response (below). The same separator is used in .action files.
You ran catkin_make in ~/catkin_ws. In a new terminal, rosrun cannot find your new package. What is missing?
Running source ~/catkin_ws/devel/setup.bash
Running rospack rebuild in the workspace
Adding the package to ROS_MASTER_URI
Restarting roscore with the --reload flag
Sourcing the workspace's setup file adds it to ROS_PACKAGE_PATH and other variables. Sourcing only /opt/ros/<distro>/setup.bash does not include your workspace.
Which two files must every catkin package contain?
package.xml and CMakeLists.txt
setup.py and launch.xml
manifest.yaml and Makefile
package.json and CMakeLists.txt
package.xml holds the metadata and dependencies, and CMakeLists.txt defines the build. setup.py is optional and only needed for Python modules.
What is the main build difference between catkin_make and catkin build (from catkin_tools)?
catkin build builds each package in isolation; catkin_make uses one CMake project
catkin_make builds each package in isolation; catkin build uses one CMake project
catkin build only works for Python packages; catkin_make only for C++
catkin_make supports parallel jobs; catkin build compiles packages one by one
catkin_make combines all packages into a single CMake invocation, while catkin build configures and builds each package separately, often in parallel.
A node runs as /driver in the root namespace. Which parameter does rospy.get_param("~rate") read?
/driver/rate
/rate
/global/rate
/driver/private/rate
The tilde makes a name private, so it is resolved inside the node's own namespace: /driver/rate.
A node reads a parameter once at startup with get_param. You then change it with rosparam set. What happens?
The node keeps the old value until it reads the parameter again
The node receives the new value through an automatic callback
The node restarts so it can load the new value
The parameter server rejects the change while the node runs
The parameter server is a passive store. Nodes must re-read values or use a mechanism such as dynamic_reconfigure to react to changes.
In ROS 1, what happens if you run roslaunch while no roscore is running?
roslaunch starts a roscore automatically
roslaunch exits with an error about the Master
The nodes start but wait silently for a Master
roslaunch asks for a remote Master address
If no Master is reachable at ROS_MASTER_URI, roslaunch starts one itself, which is convenient for single-machine setups.
In a ROS launch file, which tag makes a node subscribe to /scan_front instead of /scan without changing its code?
<remap from="scan" to="scan_front"/>
<arg name="scan" value="scan_front"/>
<param name="scan" value="scan_front"/>
<group ns="scan" to="scan_front"/>
remap renames a topic name used inside the node. arg is a launch-file variable and param sets a value on the parameter server.
A launch file declares <arg name="robot" default="r1"/>. How do you set it to r2 from the command line?
roslaunch my_pkg demo.launch robot:=r2
roslaunch my_pkg demo.launch --robot=r2
roslaunch my_pkg demo.launch _robot:=r2
roslaunch my_pkg demo.launch robot=r2
Launch arguments use the name:=value syntax. The underscore form _name:=value sets a private parameter when using rosrun.
Two tf publishers both broadcast base_link as a child: one of odom, the other of map. What is the problem?
A tf frame can have only one parent, so the tree is broken
tf requires every frame to have exactly two parents
base_link is reserved and cannot be a child frame
tf only allows transforms published by one node
tf frames must form a tree. The usual convention is map to odom to base_link, where localization publishes map to odom.
In tf2, what does passing rospy.Time(0) as the time argument of lookup_transform request?
The latest available transform in the buffer
The transform at the moment the node started
The transform at Unix time zero (1970)
A transform predicted slightly into the future
Time(0) is a special value meaning 'latest available'. Using now() instead can fail if the transform has not arrived yet.
A camera is bolted to a robot at a fixed offset. Which tool publishes that transform from the command line, without code or a URDF?
static_transform_publisher from tf2_ros
tf_echo from tf
view_frames from tf2_tools
rqt_tf_tree from rqt
static_transform_publisher broadcasts a fixed transform. tf_echo prints transforms, and view_frames and rqt_tf_tree visualize the tree.
You replay a recorded bag with rosbag play --clock. What should nodes use so they follow the bag's time?
Set the /use_sim_time parameter to true before starting them
Set ROS_MASTER_URI to the bag's recorded Master
Pass the --realtime flag to every node
Run rosbag reindex before playing the bag
With use_sim_time true, nodes read time from /clock, which rosbag play --clock publishes. Otherwise timestamps and wall time disagree.
Which command prints the duration, topics, message types and message counts of a ROS 1 bag file?
rosbag info
rosbag stats
rosbag show
rosbag describe
rosbag info gives a summary of a bag file. The other subcommands do not exist.
isaac-sim: NVIDIA Isaac Sim is built on top of which NVIDIA platform?
NVIDIA Omniverse (Kit)
NVIDIA DRIVE OS
NVIDIA Jetson Linux
NVIDIA Riva
Isaac Sim is an Omniverse Kit application, so it inherits USD scenes, RTX rendering and the extension system.
What is the native scene and asset format used by Isaac Sim?
OpenUSD (Universal Scene Description)
SDF (Simulation Description Format)
URDF (Unified Robot Description Format)
MJCF (MuJoCo XML format)
Everything in Isaac Sim lives on a USD stage. URDF, MJCF and similar formats are converted to USD by importers.
Which physics engine does Isaac Sim use for rigid bodies, articulations and contacts?
NVIDIA PhysX
ODE (Open Dynamics Engine)
Bullet Physics
MuJoCo
Isaac Sim uses NVIDIA PhysX, which can run on the GPU for large batches of simulated robots.
In an Isaac Sim standalone Python script, why must SimulationApp be created before importing most omni or isaacsim modules?
Those modules need the Kit app and its extensions to be loaded first
SimulationApp downloads the modules from Nucleus at startup
Python imports are disabled until the GPU driver is checked
The modules are compiled to bytecode by SimulationApp
Isaac Sim modules are provided by Kit extensions, which only exist after SimulationApp starts the Kit runtime.
In a binary (workstation) install of Isaac Sim, which helper runs a standalone script with the bundled Python environment?
./python.sh my_script.py
./omni.sh my_script.py
pip run isaacsim my_script.py
ros2 run isaac_sim my_script.py
The python.sh wrapper in the Isaac Sim folder sets up paths and runs the bundled interpreter. The other commands are not Isaac Sim tools.
In Isaac Sim, how is functionality such as importers, sensors and ROS bridges packaged and enabled?
As Kit extensions, toggled in the Extension Manager
As Docker containers, started from the Content browser
As separate executables, launched from the terminal
As USD layers, enabled in the Stage panel
Omniverse Kit apps are made of extensions. Isaac Sim features are enabled or disabled as extensions.
A PhysX joint drive computes force = stiffness * (target position - position) + damping * (target velocity - velocity). How do you set up pure velocity control?
Set stiffness to 0 and damping to a positive value
Set damping to 0 and stiffness to a positive value
Set both stiffness and damping to large values
Set both stiffness and damping to 0
With stiffness 0, the position error term disappears and the damping term drives the joint toward the target velocity. Both at 0 gives no drive force at all.
Why are robot arms in Isaac Sim usually simulated as articulations rather than separate rigid bodies linked by joints?
The reduced-coordinate solver keeps chains accurate and stable
Articulations skip collision checks, so they run faster
Separate rigid bodies cannot be rendered by RTX
Articulations allow joints without any physical limits
Articulations use a reduced-coordinate formulation, so joints do not drift apart and long chains stay stable, unlike maximal-coordinate joint constraints.
In Isaac Sim, your imported robot falls straight through the ground plane when you press Play. What is the most likely cause?
The robot links or the ground have no collision (Collision API) applied
Gravity is set to a positive value along the z axis
The RTX renderer is in path tracing mode
The stage units are set to centimeters
Rigid bodies only interact when their prims have colliders. Without collision geometry, physics lets them pass through each other.
You add a robot USD file to your scene as a reference and change one joint's stiffness in your stage. What happens to the robot's source file?
Nothing: the change is stored as an opinion in your stage's layer
The source file is rewritten with the new stiffness
The edit is rejected because referenced prims are read-only
The reference is converted into a full copy of the robot
USD composition is non-destructive. Local edits are stronger opinions in your layer and override the referenced asset without modifying it.
When importing a URDF robot arm that should be bolted to a table, which importer option should you enable?
Fix Base Link
Merge Fixed Joints
Self Collision
Create Physics Scene
Fix Base Link anchors the root link to the world. Without it, the arm's base is free and the robot can tip over or fall.
What does the Merge Fixed Joints option of the Isaac Sim URDF importer do?
Combines links joined by fixed joints into a single rigid body
Converts fixed joints into revolute joints with tight limits
Deletes all links that have no visual meshes
Locks every joint so the robot cannot move
Merging fixed joints reduces the number of bodies, which simplifies and speeds up the simulation without changing the robot's motion.
A gripper's fingers have concave meshes. Which collision approximation keeps their shape best in PhysX?
Convex decomposition
Convex hull
Bounding sphere
Bounding cube
A convex hull fills in concave regions, so fingers cannot grasp properly. Convex decomposition splits the mesh into several convex pieces.
Besides URDF, Isaac Sim ships an importer for which MuJoCo robot description format?
MJCF
SDF
COLLADA
STEP
Isaac Sim includes an MJCF importer that converts MuJoCo XML models to USD.
Which Omniverse framework does Isaac Sim use to generate labeled synthetic images with randomized scenes?
Omniverse Replicator
Isaac Lab
Omniverse Nucleus
Isaac ROS
Replicator provides randomizers, writers and annotators for synthetic data. Isaac Lab is for robot learning.
Why do synthetic data pipelines randomize lighting, textures, camera poses and object placement?
To help models trained on simulation work on real images
To reduce the file size of the generated dataset
To make the RTX renderer run at a higher frame rate
To avoid needing labels for the generated images
Domain randomization exposes the model to wide variation, so the real world looks like one more variation. This improves sim-to-real transfer.
In Replicator, the bounding_box_2d_tight output is empty even though objects are visible. What is the most likely cause?
The objects have no semantic labels assigned
The camera uses the path tracing renderer
The objects have no physics colliders
The stage is saved in .usda instead of .usdc
Annotators such as bounding boxes and segmentation report only prims that carry semantic labels.
Which Isaac Sim annotator gives per-pixel class labels for training a segmentation network?
semantic_segmentation
distance_to_camera
motion_vectors
normals
semantic_segmentation assigns each pixel a class ID based on semantic labels. The other annotators give depth, motion or surface direction.
Which NVIDIA framework built on Isaac Sim is the recommended successor to Isaac Gym for robot learning?
Isaac Lab
Isaac Cortex
Omniverse Replicator
Isaac Mission Dispatch
Isaac Lab (which grew out of Orbit) replaces the deprecated Isaac Gym preview for reinforcement and imitation learning.
Why can Isaac Lab train reinforcement learning policies much faster than a typical CPU simulator loop?
It runs thousands of environments in parallel on the GPU
It skips physics and replays recorded robot motions
It lowers the control rate to one action per second
It trains on low-resolution images instead of states
GPU physics and tensor APIs step many environments at once and keep data on the GPU, avoiding slow CPU to GPU copies.
gazebo: Which XML format does Gazebo use natively to describe worlds and models?
SDF (Simulation Description Format)
URDF (Unified Robot Description Format)
MJCF (MuJoCo XML format)
USD (Universal Scene Description)
Gazebo uses SDF for worlds, models, sensors and plugins. URDF files are converted to SDF when loaded.
In an SDF world file, which element contains the models, lights and physics settings of the simulation?
<world>
<model>
<scene>
<link>
The <world> element holds everything in the simulation. <scene> only sets visual properties like ambient light and background.
What does <static>true</static> do inside an SDF model?
The model does not move under physics but other objects can collide with it
The model is removed from collision checks but still falls under gravity
The model is rendered without lighting or shadows
The model's pose is reset at every simulation step
Static models are fixed in place, which suits buildings and terrain. They still provide collision surfaces.
In Gazebo Classic, a world includes <uri>model://my_robot</uri> and fails to load it. Which variable should list the folder that holds my_robot?
GAZEBO_MODEL_PATH
GAZEBO_PLUGIN_PATH
ROS_PACKAGE_PATH
GAZEBO_MASTER_URI
model:// URIs are resolved against GAZEBO_MODEL_PATH. GAZEBO_PLUGIN_PATH is for plugin libraries.
In Gazebo, which roles do gzserver and gzclient play?
gzserver runs physics and sensors; gzclient is the graphical interface
gzserver is the graphical interface; gzclient runs physics and sensors
gzserver stores models online; gzclient downloads them
gzserver runs ROS nodes; gzclient runs Gazebo plugins
The server does the simulation and can run headless. The client only visualizes and lets you interact.
Which physics engine does Gazebo Classic use by default?
ODE
Bullet
DART
Simbody
Gazebo Classic defaults to ODE and also supports Bullet, Simbody and DART. Modern Gazebo (gz sim) defaults to DART.
In a Gazebo Classic world file, how do you switch the physics engine to Bullet?
<physics type="bullet">
<engine name="bullet">
<world physics="bullet">
<plugin name="bullet">
The type attribute of the <physics> element selects the engine. The engine must also be compiled into your Gazebo build.
A Gazebo Classic world sets max_step_size to 0.001 and real_time_update_rate to 1000. What real time factor is targeted?
The target real time factor is max_step_size times real_time_update_rate: 0.001 s per step times 1000 steps per second gives 1.0.
A Gazebo robot model jitters, explodes or flies away as soon as the simulation starts. What is a common cause?
Unrealistic mass or inertia values on its links
Too many lights in the world file
A camera sensor with a low update rate
A model.config file without an author tag
Tiny or inconsistent inertia tensors make the solver unstable. Correct inertials, or a smaller step size, usually fix it.
Which SDF sensor type simulates a laser scanner on the GPU in Gazebo Classic?
gpu_ray
depth
contact
imu
In Gazebo Classic, ray is the CPU laser and gpu_ray is the GPU version. Modern Gazebo calls it gpu_lidar.
In an SDF camera sensor, what unit does <horizontal_fov> use?
Radians
Degrees
Pixels
Millimeters
SDF angles are in radians. A value of 1.047 is about 60 degrees.
A Gazebo lidar uses 360 horizontal samples with min_angle -3.14159 and max_angle 3.14159. What is the approximate angular resolution?
About 1 degree per sample
About 0.1 degree per sample
About 3.6 degrees per sample
About 10 degrees per sample
The scan covers about 2 pi radians (360 degrees) with 360 samples, so each beam is about 1 degree apart.
How do you make a simulated Gazebo camera or lidar produce more realistic data?
Add a <noise> element, for example type gaussian with a stddev
Lower the <update_rate> to 1 Hz
Mark the sensor model as <static>
Switch the physics engine to Bullet
Real sensors are noisy. A gaussian <noise> block with mean and stddev makes training and testing more honest.
In Gazebo Classic, which plugin type should you write to control the joints of one specific robot?
A model plugin
A world plugin
A GUI plugin
A system plugin
Model plugins attach to a single model and get access to its links and joints. World plugins act on the whole world.
In a Gazebo Classic C++ model plugin, which macro makes the class loadable by the simulator?
GZ_REGISTER_MODEL_PLUGIN(MyPlugin)
GZ_LOAD_PLUGIN(MyPlugin)
PLUGINLIB_EXPORT_CLASS(MyPlugin)
GAZEBO_PLUGIN_INIT(MyPlugin)
GZ_REGISTER_MODEL_PLUGIN registers the class with Gazebo. PLUGINLIB_EXPORT_CLASS is a ROS pluginlib macro, not a Gazebo one.
A Gazebo Classic plugin's SDF block contains <gain>2.5</gain>. How does the plugin read it?
From the sdf::ElementPtr passed to Load, e.g. sdf->Get<double>("gain")
From a ROS parameter called /gazebo/gain
From an environment variable named GAIN
From the model.config file of the model
Load receives the plugin's SDF element, so custom child tags act as plugin parameters.
A Gazebo Classic model plugin must apply a force at every simulation step. What is the usual approach?
Connect a callback with event::Events::ConnectWorldUpdateBegin
Start a thread that sleeps for 1 ms in a loop
Call the force code once inside the plugin constructor
Use a ROS timer at the same rate as the GUI
The world update event fires on every physics step, so the callback stays synchronized with simulation time.
Using ROS 2 with modern Gazebo (gz sim), which package relays messages between Gazebo topics and ROS 2 topics?
ros_gz_bridge
gazebo_ros_pkgs
rosbridge_server
image_transport
ros_gz_bridge converts between gz-transport and ROS 2 messages. gazebo_ros_pkgs is for Gazebo Classic.
Which plugin lets ros2_control controllers command the joints of a robot simulated in Gazebo Classic?
gazebo_ros2_control
gazebo_ros_camera
gazebo_ros_ray_sensor
gazebo_ros_state
gazebo_ros2_control exposes the simulated joints as ros2_control hardware interfaces. The others are sensor or state plugins.
What is the default port of the Gazebo Classic master in GAZEBO_MASTER_URI?
Gazebo Classic uses port 11345. Port 11311 belongs to the ROS 1 Master, a common source of confusion.
mujoco: What is the root element of a MuJoCo MJCF model file?
<mujoco>
<robot>
<sdf>
<world>
MJCF files start with <mujoco>. <robot> is the URDF root and <sdf> is the SDF root.
What is the default simulation timestep in MuJoCo when <option> does not set one?
0.002 seconds
0.001 seconds
0.01 seconds
1/240 seconds
MuJoCo defaults to 2 ms. The value 1/240 s is PyBullet's default.
In MJCF, a child <body> contains geoms but no <joint>. How does it move relative to its parent?
It is welded to its parent and moves with it rigidly
It gets a free joint and falls under gravity
It gets a hinge joint around its z axis
It is ignored by the physics simulation
Joints create degrees of freedom between a body and its parent. With no joint, the body has zero degrees of freedom relative to the parent.
A MuJoCo model contains only one body attached to the world with a free joint. What are model.nq and model.nv?
nq = 7 and nv = 6
nq = 6 and nv = 6
nq = 7 and nv = 7
nq = 6 and nv = 7
A free joint stores position (3) plus a unit quaternion (4) in qpos, but has only 6 velocity degrees of freedom.
In what component order does MuJoCo store quaternions, for example in qpos or a body's quat attribute?
w, x, y, z
x, y, z, w
x, w, y, z
z, y, x, w
MuJoCo puts the scalar part first. PyBullet and ROS use x, y, z, w, so conversions are a common bug source.
Using the official mujoco Python bindings, which call advances the simulation by one timestep?
mujoco.mj_step(model, data)
mujoco.mj_forward(model, data)
mujoco.mj_resetData(model, data)
data.step(model)
mj_step integrates the dynamics by one timestep. mj_forward computes derived quantities without advancing time.
You write new values into data.qpos and need data.xpos (body positions) updated without advancing time. Which function do you call?
mujoco.mj_forward
mujoco.mj_step
mujoco.mj_inverse
mujoco.mj_resetData
mj_forward recomputes kinematics and forces for the current state without integrating. mj_step would also move time forward.
Which MuJoCo function computes the generalized forces needed to produce a given acceleration data.qacc?
mujoco.mj_inverse
mujoco.mj_forward
mujoco.mj_step
mujoco.mj_fullM
mj_inverse runs inverse dynamics and writes the result to data.qfrc_inverse. mj_fullM converts the sparse mass matrix to dense form.
In MuJoCo, what does data.qfrc_bias contain?
Coriolis, centrifugal and gravity forces in joint space
Forces from actuators after applying the gear ratio
Contact forces in the world frame for each geom
User-applied external forces on each body
MuJoCo writes the dynamics as M qacc + bias = applied forces; qfrc_bias is the velocity- and gravity-dependent term c(q, qvel).
In MuJoCo Python, where do you write the commands that drive the model's actuators?
data.ctrl
data.qfrc_applied
model.actuator_gear
data.act
data.ctrl holds one control value per actuator. qfrc_applied adds raw generalized forces and bypasses actuators.
You want an MJCF actuator that drives a joint toward a commanded angle. Which actuator element fits best?
<position joint="elbow" kp="100"/>
<motor joint="elbow" gear="100"/>
<velocity joint="elbow" kv="100"/>
<general joint="elbow" gear="100"/>
A position actuator applies a force proportional to the angle error, like a servo. A motor applies force proportional to ctrl directly.
Two MuJoCo geoms both have contype="1" and conaffinity="0". Can they collide with each other?
No, because neither contype matches the other's conaffinity
Yes, because their contype values are equal
Yes, but only if they belong to the same body
No, because contype must be larger than 1
A contact is generated only if (contype1 & conaffinity2) or (contype2 & conaffinity1) is nonzero. Here both tests give 0.
Which MuJoCo condim value produces frictionless contacts?
condim 1 models only the normal force. The default 3 adds sliding friction, 4 adds torsional and 6 adds rolling friction.
Which MJCF geom attributes mainly control how stiff and damped MuJoCo's soft contacts are?
solref and solimp
contype and conaffinity
rgba and group
margin and gap only
MuJoCo contacts are soft constraints. solref sets time constant and damping ratio, and solimp sets impedance versus penetration.
Why do the geoms of two adjacent bodies in a MuJoCo chain (parent and child) not collide with each other by default?
MuJoCo filters out contacts between a body and its parent
MuJoCo only checks contacts between geoms of type plane
Adjacent bodies share one geom, so no pair exists
Contacts are only enabled after mj_inverse is called
Contacts between geoms in the same body or in a parent and child body are excluded by default, since joints usually make them overlap.
What is a key benefit of MuJoCo simulating in generalized (joint) coordinates?
Joint constraints hold by construction, so links never drift apart
Contacts are computed without any numerical tolerance
Every body has exactly six degrees of freedom
The mass matrix is constant for the whole run
Each joint adds only its own degrees of freedom, so joints do not need to be enforced as extra constraints that can be violated.
A model with strong joint damping becomes unstable with the default Euler integrator. Which <option> integrator setting is designed to help?
implicitfast
RK4 with a larger timestep
Euler with damping disabled
explicit
Implicit integrators (implicit, implicitfast) treat velocity-dependent forces such as damping implicitly, which improves stability.
Which of these is a standard Gymnasium environment that runs on MuJoCo?
HalfCheetah
CartPole
LunarLander
Breakout
HalfCheetah, Hopper, Ant and Humanoid are Gymnasium MuJoCo tasks. CartPole is classic control, LunarLander uses Box2D, Breakout is Atari.
A Gymnasium MuJoCo environment has a model timestep of 0.01 s and frame_skip of 5. How much simulated time passes per env.step()?
Each env.step applies the action and calls the MuJoCo step frame_skip times, so 5 x 0.01 s = 0.05 s.
What is MJX in the MuJoCo project?
A JAX version of MuJoCo for batched simulation on GPU or TPU
A file format that compresses MJCF models for sharing
A web viewer that renders MuJoCo models in a browser
A ROS package that bridges MuJoCo topics to ROS 2
MJX reimplements MuJoCo in JAX, so many environments can run in parallel on accelerators, which is useful for RL.
pybullet: What is PyBullet?
A Python module that wraps the Bullet Physics SDK
A Python port of the MuJoCo physics engine
A ROS package that renders Gazebo worlds in Python
A Python front end for NVIDIA PhysX on the GPU
PyBullet exposes Bullet Physics to Python for simulation, robotics and RL, with optional OpenGL visualization.
You need to run PyBullet on a server without a display. Which connection mode should you use?
p.connect(p.DIRECT)
p.connect(p.GUI)
p.connect(p.SHARED_MEMORY)
p.connect(p.GUI_SERVER)
DIRECT runs physics in the same process with no window. GUI opens an OpenGL window, which needs a display.
p.loadURDF("plane.urdf") fails with 'Cannot load URDF file'. What is the usual fix?
Call p.setAdditionalSearchPath(pybullet_data.getDataPath()) first
Call p.setGravity(0, 0, -9.81) before loading
Pass useFixedBase=True to loadURDF
Connect with p.GUI instead of p.DIRECT
plane.urdf ships in the pybullet_data package. Adding its folder to the search path lets loadURDF find it.
In PyBullet, you load a cube, call p.stepSimulation() in a loop, and the cube just floats. Why?
Gravity is zero by default until you call p.setGravity
The cube's mass defaults to zero in every URDF
stepSimulation only updates the GUI, not the physics
Objects sleep until a contact wakes them up
PyBullet starts with zero gravity. Calling p.setGravity(0, 0, -9.81) makes objects fall.
With default settings, how much simulated time passes after 240 calls to p.stepSimulation()?
1 second
0.24 seconds
2.4 seconds
4 seconds
The default time step is 1/240 s, so 240 steps make 1 second. You can change it with p.setTimeStep.
Which p.loadURDF argument keeps a robot arm's base anchored to the world?
useFixedBase=True
globalScaling=0
useMaximalCoordinates=True
flags=p.URDF_USE_INERTIA_FROM_FILE
useFixedBase=True gives the base zero mass in the simulation so it stays in place.
In PyBullet, which link index refers to a multibody's base?
None
The base has index -1. Link indices 0 to getNumJoints() - 1 match the joints that connect each child link.
How do you find the index of the joint named "elbow" in a PyBullet robot?
Loop over range(p.getNumJoints(robot)) and check p.getJointInfo(robot, i)[1]
Call p.getJointIndex(robot, "elbow") directly
Read the index from p.getBasePositionAndOrientation(robot)
Use the order of joints printed by p.getDynamicsInfo(robot, -1)
getJointInfo returns a tuple whose second item is the joint name (as bytes). There is no built-in lookup by name.
What does p.calculateInverseKinematics(robot, eeLink, targetPos) return?
Joint positions, one for each movable (non-fixed) joint
The end effector's position and orientation
The joint torques needed to hold the target pose
A boolean saying whether the target is reachable
It returns a list with one value per degree of freedom. Fixed joints are skipped, so the list can be shorter than getNumJoints.
You call p.calculateInverseKinematics and get valid joint values, but the robot does not move. What is missing?
Sending the values to the joints, e.g. with setJointMotorControlArray, and stepping
Calling p.calculateInverseKinematics a second time
Setting the robot's base mass to zero
Enabling self collision on the URDF
IK only computes a solution. You still have to command the motors and step the simulation.
Which call gives the current world position of a link frame after you change joint angles with resetJointState?
p.getLinkState(robot, link, computeForwardKinematics=True)
p.getJointState(robot, link)
p.getBasePositionAndOrientation(robot)
p.getDynamicsInfo(robot, link)
getLinkState returns the link's Cartesian pose. computeForwardKinematics=True makes it recompute the pose from the current joint values.
In p.setJointMotorControl2 with p.POSITION_CONTROL, what does the force argument set?
The maximum motor force or torque used to reach the target
A constant torque added on top of the position command
The stiffness gain of the position controller
The force at which the joint breaks off the robot
The motor tries to reach targetPosition but never applies more than force. Gains are set with positionGain and velocityGain.
You want pure torque control of a revolute joint in PyBullet, but TORQUE_CONTROL seems to have no effect. What must you do first?
Disable the default motor with VELOCITY_CONTROL and force=0
Set the joint's lateral friction to zero
Call p.resetJointState with targetValue=0
Load the URDF with useFixedBase=False
PyBullet joints have a default velocity motor that resists motion. Setting its force to 0 frees the joint for torque commands.
What does p.resetJointState do?
Instantly sets a joint's angle, ignoring dynamics
Smoothly moves a joint to an angle using its motor
Resets the joint's motor gains to default values
Clears all forces applied to the joint this step
resetJointState teleports the joint. It is meant for setting up initial poses, not for control during simulation.
You move two objects so they overlap with resetBasePositionAndOrientation, then call p.getContactPoints, which returns nothing. Why?
Contact points are computed during stepSimulation
getContactPoints only works in GUI mode
Objects must be loaded with useFixedBase=True
getContactPoints reports only self collisions
getContactPoints reads results from the last simulation step. Step once, or use getClosestPoints, which runs a query immediately.
How can you check whether a gripper is within 5 cm of an object without needing an actual contact?
p.getClosestPoints(gripper, obj, distance=0.05)
p.getContactPoints(gripper, obj, distance=0.05)
p.rayTest(gripper, obj, 0.05)
p.getOverlappingObjects(gripper, 0.05)
getClosestPoints returns point pairs closer than the given distance, computed right away, even when the bodies do not touch.
By default, do links of the same PyBullet robot collide with each other?
No, unless you load it with flags=p.URDF_USE_SELF_COLLISION
Yes, unless you load it with flags=p.URDF_IGNORE_SELF
Yes, but only links that share a fixed joint
No, and self collision cannot be enabled
Self collision is off by default for URDF bodies and must be enabled with the URDF_USE_SELF_COLLISION flag.
Which PyBullet function disables collisions between one specific link of robot A and one link of robot B?
p.setCollisionFilterPair
p.setCollisionFilterGroupMask
p.changeVisualShape
p.removeConstraint
setCollisionFilterPair enables or disables collision between two specific links. The group mask version filters whole groups.
Which PyBullet functions are commonly used to simulate a laser range finder?
p.rayTest and p.rayTestBatch
p.getClosestPoints and p.getAABB
p.getCameraImage and p.computeViewMatrix
p.getContactPoints and p.getLinkState
Ray tests cast lines into the scene and return the first hit, which is what a lidar beam measures. rayTestBatch handles many rays at once.
In what order does p.getQuaternionFromEuler return quaternion components?
x, y, z, w
w, x, y, z
w, z, y, x
x, w, y, z
PyBullet uses x, y, z, w with the scalar last, unlike MuJoCo, which puts w first.
omniverse: Which company originally developed USD (Universal Scene Description), the format at the core of Omniverse?
Pixar
NVIDIA
Autodesk
Epic Games
Pixar created USD and open-sourced it in 2016. NVIDIA built Omniverse around it.
Which USD file extension is a human-readable text format?
.usda
.usdc
.usdz
.usdb
.usda is ASCII text, .usdc is the binary crate format and .usdz is a zip package. .usdb is not a USD format.
A prim gets size = 2 from a referenced file, and your root layer sets size = 5 directly on it. Which value is used?
5, because local opinions are the strongest
2, because references override local edits
The average of both values
An error, since two opinions conflict
In USD's LIVRPS strength order, Local opinions come first and win over References.
What is the main reason to bring a heavy asset into a USD stage as a payload instead of a reference?
Payloads can be unloaded so the stage opens faster
Payloads copy the asset into the stage file
Payloads let the asset be edited by several users
Payloads convert the asset to the binary format
Payloads are references that can be loaded or unloaded on demand, which keeps large scenes manageable.
In USD Python, what does UsdGeom.Cube.Define(stage, "/World/Box") do?
Creates a Cube prim at /World/Box, or returns it if it already exists
Loads a cube mesh from the file named /World/Box
Renders a cube at /World/Box for one frame only
Checks whether /World/Box has a Cube type and returns a bool
Define authors a prim of that schema type at the given path, also creating missing parent prims.
A USD chair asset must offer red, blue and green versions that users can switch between. Which USD feature fits?
A variant set
A sublayer per color
A relationship per color
A separate stage per color
Variant sets store several alternatives inside one asset and let the user pick one, such as color or level of detail.
In USD, how is a material bound to a mesh prim?
Through a relationship that targets the material prim
Through an attribute holding the material's color
Through a sublayer containing the material
Through a variant set named material
Material binding uses the material:binding relationship. Relationships point to other prims, while attributes hold values.
Omniverse's RTX renderer offers a Real-Time mode and a path tracing mode. When is the Real-Time mode the better choice?
Interactive navigation of large scenes at high frame rates
Final frames that need the most accurate global illumination
Reference renders that are compared with offline results
Still images where render time does not matter
Real-Time uses ray-traced effects with approximations for speed. Path tracing is slower but more physically accurate.
Which material language is used by the Omniverse RTX renderer for physically based materials?
MDL (NVIDIA Material Definition Language)
GLSL (OpenGL Shading Language)
OSL (Open Shading Language)
HLSL (High-Level Shading Language)
Omniverse materials are written in MDL, which describes physically based materials independently of the renderer.
In Omniverse RTX, what does enabling DLSS do?
Renders at a lower resolution and upscales with AI for higher frame rates
Adds extra light bounces for more accurate reflections
Compresses textures so the scene uses less disk space
Synchronizes the viewport with other Nucleus users
DLSS uses a neural network on RTX GPUs to reconstruct a high-resolution image from a lower-resolution render.
Which URL scheme points to a file stored on an Omniverse Nucleus server?
omniverse://server/path/scene.usd
nucleus://server/path/scene.usd
usd://server/path/scene.usd
kit://server/path/scene.usd
Nucleus paths use the omniverse:// scheme. The other schemes are not used by Omniverse.
What is the role of a Nucleus server in Omniverse?
It stores USD content and lets several apps and users share it
It renders frames on the GPU for every connected client
It compiles Kit extensions into native binaries
It runs PhysX simulations for all connected apps
Nucleus is the database and collaboration engine: it stores assets, handles access and syncs changes between clients.
A team needs to go back to the version of a USD file saved last week on Nucleus. Which Nucleus feature helps?
Checkpoints
Variant sets
Payloads
Session layers
Nucleus checkpoints keep saved versions of a file that can be restored. Variant sets and payloads are USD features, not version history.
Two artists in different Omniverse-connected apps want to see each other's edits to one scene almost immediately. What enables this?
A live session on Nucleus that syncs USD changes
Exporting the scene as .usdz after every edit
Rendering the scene with the path tracer
Converting the stage to a single flattened layer
Live sessions send small USD deltas through Nucleus so all connected clients stay in sync.
In an Omniverse Kit extension, which file declares its name, version and dependencies?
extension.toml
package.json
setup.cfg
manifest.xml
Each Kit extension has a config/extension.toml with metadata, dependencies and Python module settings.
A Python Kit extension class subclasses omni.ext.IExt. Which methods does Kit call when the extension is enabled and disabled?
on_startup(ext_id) and on_shutdown()
__init__() and __del__()
start() and stop()
load(ext_id) and unload()
Kit calls on_startup when the extension is enabled and on_shutdown when it is disabled, so UI and subscriptions can be cleaned up.
Your Kit extension uses omni.ui. How do you make sure omni.ui is loaded before your extension starts?
List omni.ui under [dependencies] in extension.toml
Import omni.ui at the top of every Python file
Rename the extension so it sorts after omni.ui
Add omni.ui to the Python requirements.txt
Kit resolves the [dependencies] section and starts required extensions first. An import alone does not enable an extension.
In Omniverse, what is a Connector?
A plugin that exchanges data between a third-party tool and USD or Nucleus
A cable standard for linking RTX GPUs in one workstation
A USD relationship that links two prims in a scene
A PhysX joint that attaches two rigid bodies
Connectors let tools such as CAD or DCC apps publish to and read from Omniverse, which is key for digital twins.
In a factory digital twin built on Omniverse, how should live sensor readings reach the 3D scene?
A service or extension subscribes to the data and writes it to USD attributes
An artist re-exports the factory model every time a value changes
The RTX renderer reads the sensors directly from the network
Nucleus polls each sensor and creates a new checkpoint per value
A digital twin needs a data pipeline that maps real-time signals to scene properties, so the twin reflects the real system.
Why is USD layering useful when several teams build one digital twin?
Each team edits its own layer without overwriting the others
Layers merge all edits into a single file automatically
Layers lock the stage so only one team edits at a time
Layers convert every asset to the same polygon count
Layers stack non-destructively. Layout, lighting and simulation teams can work in parallel and compose results on one stage.
slam: In EKF-SLAM, what does the state vector contain?
The robot pose and the positions of all mapped landmarks
Only the robot pose, with landmarks in a separate file
Only landmark positions relative to the first robot pose
Raw sensor readings from the last few time steps
EKF-SLAM estimates robot pose and landmarks jointly, with a full covariance matrix that captures their correlations.
How does the cost of one EKF-SLAM update grow with the number of landmarks n?
Roughly O(n^2), because the full covariance is updated
Roughly O(1), because only the robot pose changes
Roughly O(log n), using a landmark index
Roughly O(n^3) only at loop closures
The covariance matrix is n by n, and each update touches all of it. This limits EKF-SLAM to small maps.
In graph-based SLAM, what do nodes and edges usually represent?
Nodes are poses (or landmarks); edges are measurement constraints
Nodes are sensor readings; edges are timestamps
Nodes are grid cells; edges are free-space rays
Nodes are features; edges are image pixels
Graph SLAM builds a pose graph and finds the poses that best satisfy all constraints.
How is the optimal pose graph usually found in graph-based SLAM?
Nonlinear least squares, e.g. Gauss-Newton or Levenberg-Marquardt
A single Kalman filter prediction step
Breadth-first search over the graph
K-means clustering of the robot poses
The graph defines a sum of squared errors that solvers such as g2o, GTSAM or Ceres minimize iteratively.
Which of these libraries is commonly used to optimize pose graphs in SLAM?
GTSAM
OctoMap
MoveIt
tf2
GTSAM (like g2o and Ceres) solves factor graph optimization. OctoMap is a 3D mapping structure, MoveIt is for motion planning.
What is loop closure in SLAM?
Recognizing a previously visited place and adding a constraint to it
Stopping the robot when the map has no unknown cells
Returning the robot to its start pose after mapping
Closing gaps between scan points with interpolation
A loop closure links the current pose to an earlier one, which corrects drift accumulated by odometry.
A SLAM system accepts a false loop closure between two similar-looking corridors. What is the likely effect?
The optimized map gets badly distorted
Only the newest pose shifts by a few centimeters
The system ignores it because the edge is new
Drift is reduced, just like with a real closure
A wrong constraint pulls unrelated parts of the map together. Geometric checks and robust kernels help reject such outliers.
How does ORB-SLAM find loop closure candidates?
With a bag-of-words place recognition database (DBoW2)
By running ICP against every previous keyframe
By comparing GPS positions of the keyframes
By checking the occupancy grid for overlaps
ORB descriptors are quantized into visual words, so similar keyframes can be retrieved quickly before geometric verification.
In an occupancy grid map, what probability is usually assigned to a cell that has never been observed?
0.5 means 'unknown': neither free nor occupied is more likely.
Why do occupancy grid mappers usually store each cell as log-odds instead of a probability?
Bayesian updates become simple additions
Log-odds take less memory than a byte
Log-odds values stay between 0 and 1
Log-odds remove the need for a sensor model
In log-odds, each measurement adds a value, and probabilities near 0 or 1 avoid numeric problems. Unknown (p = 0.5) is log-odds 0.
A lidar beam hits an obstacle 4 m away. How does an occupancy grid mapper update the cells along that beam?
Cells before the hit become more free; the cell at the hit more occupied
All cells along the beam become more occupied
Only the cell at the hit is updated
Cells before the hit become more occupied; the hit cell more free
The beam passed through the earlier cells, so they are likely free. Ray tracing such as Bresenham's algorithm finds those cells.
Which two steps does the classic ICP algorithm repeat?
Match nearest points, then compute the best rigid transform
Detect ORB features, then match their descriptors
Build an occupancy grid, then run A* on it
Predict with a motion model, then resample particles
ICP alternates between finding correspondences and solving for the transform that minimizes their distances.
ICP fails to align two scans that start rotated about 90 degrees apart. What is the most likely reason?
ICP needs a good initial guess and can get stuck in a local minimum
ICP only works with color point clouds
ICP cannot estimate any rotation, only translation
ICP needs exactly the same number of points
Nearest-neighbor matches are wrong when the start is far off. An odometry prior or global registration should come first.
When aligning lidar scans of walls and floors, why is point-to-plane ICP often preferred over point-to-point ICP?
It usually converges in fewer iterations on flat surfaces
It does not need any nearest-neighbor search
It works without estimating a rotation
It needs no initial guess at all
Point-to-plane lets points slide along surfaces, matching the geometry better and converging faster.
Given matched 3D point pairs with known correspondences, how is the optimal rigid transform usually computed in closed form?
SVD of the cross-covariance matrix (Kabsch or Umeyama method)
Gradient descent over all possible rotations
A Fourier transform of both point sets
Solving a linear system for a 4 x 4 affine matrix
After centering both sets, the SVD of their cross-covariance gives the best rotation, and the translation follows from the centroids.
What are ORB features made of?
FAST keypoints with rotation-aware BRIEF binary descriptors
Harris corners with floating-point SIFT descriptors
Blob detections with SURF descriptors
Edge pixels with HOG descriptors
ORB is fast to compute and match because its descriptors are binary and compared with Hamming distance.
Which three main threads run in parallel in ORB-SLAM?
Tracking, local mapping and loop closing
Sensing, rendering and planning
Prediction, update and resampling
Calibration, compression and logging
Tracking localizes each frame, local mapping refines nearby keyframes, and loop closing detects and corrects loops.
A monocular visual SLAM system builds a map that looks correct but has the wrong overall size. Why?
One camera alone cannot recover absolute scale
The camera's frame rate is too low
ORB features are not scale invariant
The map was saved in the wrong units
Monocular geometry is defined up to scale. Stereo, depth, an IMU or known object sizes are needed to fix it.
A spinning lidar on a fast vehicle produces skewed scans. What is the standard fix in LiDAR SLAM?
Deskew each scan using IMU or odometry motion during the sweep
Lower the lidar's range so fewer points are recorded
Discard every second scan before matching
Convert the scans to images before matching
The sensor moves while it sweeps, so points are captured from different poses. Motion compensation removes this distortion.
Which lidar odometry method extracts edge and planar feature points and matches them separately?
LOAM
ORB-SLAM
gmapping
MonoSLAM
LOAM classifies points by local smoothness into edges and planes. ORB-SLAM and MonoSLAM are visual, gmapping is a particle filter.
motion-planning: In motion planning, what is the configuration space (C-space) of a robot?
The set of all possible configurations of the robot
The 3D workspace volume the robot can reach
The set of all joint torques the motors can apply
The free floor area around the robot base
Each point in C-space fully describes the robot's pose. Its dimension equals the number of degrees of freedom.
A rigid robot moves on a flat floor and can translate and rotate. What is the dimension of its configuration space?
3 (x, y, theta)
4 (x, y, z, theta)
6 (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw)
Planar position needs two values and heading needs one, so the C-space is three-dimensional.
What is the dimension of the configuration space of a fixed-base robot arm with 6 revolute joints?
Each joint angle is one degree of freedom, so the C-space has 6 dimensions, regardless of the workspace being 3D.
A disc robot of radius r translates without rotating. How are obstacles usually represented in its C-space?
Each obstacle is grown by r, then the robot is treated as a point
Each obstacle is shrunk by r, then the robot is treated as a point
Obstacles keep their size, and the robot is grown by 2r
Obstacles are replaced by their bounding spheres
The C-space obstacle is the Minkowski sum of the obstacle and the robot shape, which for a disc means inflating by r.
How does Dijkstra's algorithm relate to A* search?
Dijkstra is A* with a heuristic of zero
Dijkstra is A* with an infinite heuristic
Dijkstra is A* that only expands the goal node
Dijkstra is A* run backward from the goal
A* orders nodes by g + h. With h = 0, it expands nodes by path cost only, which is exactly Dijkstra.
What property of the heuristic guarantees that A* (tree search) returns an optimal path?
It never overestimates the true remaining cost
It never underestimates the true remaining cost
It equals the number of nodes left to the goal
It increases by one with each expanded node
An admissible heuristic keeps A* optimal. A consistent heuristic also makes graph search optimal without reopening nodes.
On an 8-connected grid where diagonal moves cost sqrt(2) and straight moves cost 1, which heuristic is admissible for A*?
Euclidean distance
Manhattan distance
Manhattan distance times 1.5
Squared Euclidean distance
Euclidean distance never exceeds the true cost. Manhattan overestimates diagonal paths (2 versus about 1.41 for one diagonal step).
Weighted A* multiplies an admissible heuristic by w = 2. What do you get?
Usually faster search, with a path cost at most 2 times optimal
Slower search, but a path that is guaranteed optimal
The same search as Dijkstra, with fewer nodes stored
A path that is exactly 2 times longer than optimal
Inflating the heuristic makes the search greedier. With an admissible base heuristic, the cost is bounded by w times the optimum.
Which statement about the basic RRT algorithm is correct?
It is probabilistically complete but not asymptotically optimal
It is asymptotically optimal but not complete
It is complete and returns the shortest path
It is neither complete nor useful in high dimensions
RRT finds a path with probability approaching 1 if one exists, but the path quality does not converge to the optimum.
What does RRT* add to RRT that makes it asymptotically optimal?
Choosing the best nearby parent and rewiring neighbors
Sampling only along a straight line to the goal
Growing two trees, one from each end
Replacing random samples with a grid search
RRT* connects each new node to the lowest-cost neighbor and rewires nearby nodes through it, so path cost converges to the optimum.
Why do RRT implementations often sample the goal itself with a small probability, such as 5%?
To pull the tree toward the goal and find a path sooner
To guarantee the returned path is the shortest
To avoid checking collisions near the goal
To keep the tree from growing past a size limit
Goal biasing speeds up connection to the goal. Too much bias makes the tree greedy and worse at exploring around obstacles.
A robot must plan many paths in the same static environment with different start and goal pairs. Which sampling method fits best?
PRM (Probabilistic Roadmap)
Single-query RRT
Bidirectional RRT
Weighted A* on raw pixels
PRM builds a reusable roadmap once and answers many queries quickly. RRT variants are designed for single queries.
Why do sampling-based planners struggle with narrow passages in C-space?
Few random samples fall inside the passage
Collision checks are skipped inside passages
The passage makes the C-space lower dimensional
Samples inside the passage are discarded as duplicates
The chance of sampling a point is proportional to volume, and narrow passages have small volume. Bridge or Gaussian sampling helps.
What distinguishes a trajectory from a path in motion planning?
A trajectory also specifies timing, such as velocity over time
A trajectory is a straight line in C-space
A trajectory ignores obstacles, while a path avoids them
A trajectory is defined only in the workspace, not C-space
A path is a geometric curve. A trajectory adds a time parameterization, so velocities and accelerations are defined.
A joint trajectory must match given position, velocity and acceleration at both start and end. What is the lowest polynomial degree that can do this?
5 (quintic)
3 (cubic)
4 (quartic)
7 (septic)
There are 6 boundary conditions, so 6 coefficients are needed: a degree 5 polynomial. A cubic only matches position and velocity.
What is a typical weakness of trajectory optimization methods such as CHOMP or TrajOpt?
They can get stuck in local minima, depending on the initial guess
They can only plan for mobile robots, not arms
They ignore smoothness and only minimize length
They need a full grid of the entire C-space
These methods improve a trajectory locally using gradients. A poor start can converge to a colliding or suboptimal solution.
Why does CHOMP use a signed distance field of the environment?
It gives distances and gradients that push the trajectory away from obstacles
It stores the shortest path from every cell to the goal
It replaces collision checking with image segmentation
It converts the robot's mesh into a point cloud
The signed distance field gives smooth obstacle costs with gradients, which the optimizer follows to move points out of collision.
A planner checks collisions only at waypoints 10 cm apart and returns a path through a 2 cm thick wall. What fixes this?
Finer edge checking or continuous collision detection along segments
Increasing the spacing between checked waypoints
Checking collisions only at the start and goal
Using a larger heuristic weight in the search
Discrete checks can skip thin obstacles. Checking at a resolution smaller than the thinnest obstacle, or sweeping volumes, prevents this.
In collision checking, what is the purpose of the broad phase with bounding volumes such as AABBs or a BVH?
To cheaply reject object pairs that cannot be in contact
To compute exact contact points between meshes
To smooth the robot's path before execution
To convert concave meshes into convex ones
Bounding volume tests are fast and remove most pairs. Only the remaining pairs go to the exact narrow-phase check.
Which algorithm is widely used to compute distance or intersection between two convex shapes?
GJK (Gilbert-Johnson-Keerthi)
Bresenham's line algorithm
Dijkstra's algorithm
Marching cubes
GJK works on the Minkowski difference of two convex sets and is the core narrow-phase routine in libraries like FCL and Bullet.
